findings.issue: The new paragraph says a legacy return with a `return-rest-<id>` wallet row must not be retried, which is the guidance that was needed. The new code sends the COD remainder through payment-service under a different key, so a retry would pay it a second time. But the alternative it offers, 'Mark it REFUNDED', does not say to check two things first. (a) The `return-wallet-<id>` leg must also be present wherever the return had a wallet share. Otherwise marking the return REFUNDED by hand underpays the customer. (b) A manual status flip skips the stock release and the RETURN_REFUNDED event that finalizeRefund normally writes. This does not risk an over-refund, only an underpayment or bookkeeping gaps for an operator.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: before marking it REFUNDED, confirm the return-wallet-<id> row exists when a wallet share was expected, and release the stock and record the event by hand (or settle the whole return by hand).

summary: This is an approval: the round-2 minor is resolved and the delta adds no blocker or major. claimRefundLease is now one native UPDATE that sets refund_lease_until = now() + interval '2 minutes' with the guard status = 'PICKED_UP' AND (refund_lease_until IS NULL OR refund_lease_until < now()), and it returns the stamp with RETURNING. The stamp and the expiry check now both use the database clock, so app-server clock skew can no longer weaken the lease. @Modifying was correctly removed, because the query now returns a result set. Spring Data maps no row to Optional.empty, which OrderStore turns into null, and both callers treat null as 'do not proceed': refund() throws a 409 or returns the existing view, and resumePending returns. The explicit @Transactional makes the claim a read-write transaction of its own that commits before any money call. Release is unchanged and scoped to the holder: it runs WHERE id = :id AND refund_lease_until = :mine, using the stamp the database returned. That is a timestamptz with microsecond precision, so the value round-trips exactly. releaseIsHolderScoped (an expired holder cannot free the next caller's lease) and leaseWinsOnce cover this against the real database. The parameters are bound, so there is no injection risk. The runbook now says a legacy return with a return-rest-<id> row must not be retried on the new build, which closes the double-pay path for legacy COD and wallet-method remainders. I added one runbook minor about the manual REFUNDED alternative. Money safety: no production refund logic changed apart from the lease, and the ReturnService change only rewrites a Javadoc comment. The test changes strengthen the cap checks. concurrentSiblings now runs three siblings at once and checks that the summed wallet legs stay within W = 200 and the summed card legs within T - W = 100. A new FreezeLegsTest checks that an order already marked REFUNDED still routes a remaining return's card leg. Payment-service's refundable-balance check under its payment-row lock still bounds card and COD legs. The delta touches no endpoints, authorization, /internal token handling, logs or PII, and adds no dependencies. Note: I read the source in the F-20261119-09 worktree and did not confirm that its HEAD is b3cda340. Its content matches review-delta.diff.
